data.name: Aameen
data.gender_notes: Aameen is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic root word ‘Amin’, meaning ‘trustworthy’ or ‘reliable’. In Islam, Aameen is a name with significant spiritual meaning, representing one who is trusted and relied upon. The name Aameen carries the meaning “Trustworthy, Reliable” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Aameen usually hope their child will grow to embody trustworthy, reliable and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Aameen belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Trustworthy, Reliable.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Aameen total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

in_urdu.name: عامیں

islamic_reference.note: Traditional Islamic name with deep spiritual significance in Islamic culture

historical_references.reference: The Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) is reported to have said, 'And verily, Allah has inspired the seven heavens with this call: 'Aameen, Aameen, Aameen (yes, yes, yes).' This du'a (invocation) is a part of the Tasbeeh and is recited after every Surah (chapter) of the Quran.
The name 'Aameen' is also used in the Quran in Surah Al-A'laa, verse 13, where Allah (swt) says: 'Say: Aameen (yes) to this Qur'an. And call on your Lord with humility and in private.',
